Summarise predictor importance across people

Source: R/stats_prediction_views.R
summarize_importance.Rd

Summaries use equal weight for each person. Top-feature frequency retains all ties at the requested rank. Pooled and individual means are returned separately rather than averaged together.

Usage

summarize_importance(
  x,
  by = c("mean", "frequency"),
  model = NULL,
  scope = NULL,
  subject = NULL,
  top_n = 5L,
  method = c("coefficient", "permutation"),
  repeats = 5L
)

Arguments

x

An idiographic fit or a table returned by importance().

by

"mean" for mean importance or "frequency" for top-feature counts.

model, scope, subject

Optional filters.

top_n

Number of highest-ranked features for frequency summaries.

method, repeats

Passed to importance() when x is a fitted object.

Value

A data frame with one row per scope, model, estimator, subgroup and predictor. Includes n_subjects; frequencies also include count and percent.

Examples

fit <- fit_ml(srl, y = "effort", x = c("efficacy", "monitoring"),
              id = "name", model = "ridge", scope = "individual")
summarize_importance(fit, by = "frequency", top_n = 1)
#>        scope model estimator subgroup   variable n_subjects count  percent
#> 1 individual ridge    native    .none   efficacy         36    19 52.77778
#> 2 individual ridge    native    .none monitoring         36    17 47.22222
